54017-two-women-1862-a-poem.title: _A Poem._
54017-two-women-1862-a-poem.creator: Unknown
54017-two-women-1862-a-poem.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Ohio shines on to her border,  Ohio all golden with grain;  The river comes up at her order,  And curves toward the incoming train;  “The river! O borrow  A speed that is swifter-- Afar  Kentucky! Haste, haste, thou To-morrow!”  Poor lads, dreaming not of the sorrow,  The anguish of war.

arxiv-1803-11171.title: A metal-dielectric parabolic antenna to direct single photons
arxiv-1803-11171.creator: Sergii Morozov, Michele Gaio, Stefan A. Maier, Riccardo Sapienza
arxiv-1803-11171.description: Abstract Quantum emitters radiate light omni-directionally, making it hard to collect and use the generated photons. Here we propose a 3D metal-dielectric parabolic antenna surrounding an individual quantum dot as a source of collimated single photons which can then be easily extracted and manipulated.

arxiv-2105-10457.title: Elliptical Ordinal Embedding
arxiv-2105-10457.creator: Aïssatou Diallo, Johannes Fürnkranz
arxiv-2105-10457.description: Abstract Ordinal embedding aims at finding a low dimensional representation of objects from a set of constraints of the form ”item j j is closer to item i i than item k k ”. Typically, each object is mapped onto a point vector in a low dimensional metric space.

arxiv-2206-13593.title: Bridging atomistic spin dynamics methods and phenomenological models of single pulse ultrafast switching in ferrimagnets
arxiv-2206-13593.creator: Florian Jakobs, Unai Atxitia
arxiv-2206-13593.description: Abstract We bridge an essential knowledge gap on the understanding of all-optical ultrafast switching in ferrimagnets; namely, the connection between atomistic spin dynamics methods and macroscopic phenomenological models. All-optical switching of the magnetization occurs after the application of a single femtosecond laser pulse to specific ferrimagnetic compounds.

arxiv-2207-07683.title: First Order Logic and Twin-Width in Tournaments and Dense Oriented Graphs Thanks: Both authors were supported by the ANR projects TWIN-WIDTH (ANR-21-CE48-0014-01) and DIGRAPHS (ANR-19-CE48-0013-01). The first author was supported by the Institute for Basic Science (IBS-R029-C1).
arxiv-2207-07683.creator: Colin Geniet, Stéphan Thomassé
arxiv-2207-07683.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Colin Geniet, Stéphan Thomassé. We characterise the classes of tournaments with tractable first-order model checking. For every hereditary class of tournaments 𝒯 \mathcal{T} , first-order model checking is either fixed parameter tractable or AW ​ [ ∗ ] \textrm{AW}[*] -hard. This dichotomy coincides with the fact that 𝒯 \mathcal{T} has either bounded or unbounded twin-width, and that the growth of 𝒯 \mathcal{T} is either at most exponential or at least factorial.

arxiv-2311-14812.title: Robust Joint Estimation of Galaxy Redshift and Spectral Templates using Online Dictionary Learning
arxiv-2311-14812.creator: Sean Bryan*, Ayan Barekzai, Delondrae Carter, Philip Mauskopf, Julian Mena, Danielle Rivera, Abel S. Uriarte and Pao-Yu Wang
arxiv-2311-14812.description: Abstract We present a novel approach to analyzing astronomical spectral survey data using our non-linear extension of an online dictionary learning algorithm. Current and upcoming surveys such as SPHEREx will use spectral data to build a 3D map of the universe by estimating the redshifts of millions of galaxies.

arxiv-2503-10929.title: Constructing an Instrument as a Function of Covariates
arxiv-2503-10929.creator: Moses Stewart
arxiv-2503-10929.description: Abstract Researchers often use instrumental variables (IV) models to investigate the causal relationship between an endogenous variable and an outcome while controlling for covariates. When an exogenous variable is unavailable to serve as the instrument for an endogenous treatment, a recurring empirical practice is to construct one from a nonlinear transformation of the covariates.

arxiv-2511-11992.title: Goal-Oriented Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Decentralized Agent Teams
arxiv-2511-11992.creator: Hung Du 1 , Hy Nguyen 1 , Srikanth Thudumu 2 , Rajesh Vasa 1 , Kon Mouzakis 1
arxiv-2511-11992.description: Abstract Connected and autonomous vehicles across land, water, and air must often operate in dynamic, unpredictable environments with limited communication, no centralized control, and partial observability. These real-world constraints pose significant challenges for coordination, particularly when vehicles pursue individual objectives.

arxiv-2601-18322.title: Residual Learning for Neural Ambisonics Encoders
arxiv-2601-18322.description: Abstract Emerging wearable devices such as smartglasses and extended reality headsets demand high-quality spatial audio capture from compact, head-worn microphone arrays. Ambisonics provides a device-agnostic spatial audio representation by mapping array signals to spherical harmonic (SH) coefficients. In practice, however, accurate encoding remains challenging.

pmc-11415837.title: Advancements in adoptive CAR immune cell immunotherapy synergistically combined with multimodal approaches for tumor treatment
pmc-11415837.creator: Yun Chang, Mingyang Chang, Xiaoping Bao, Cheng Dong
pmc-11415837.description: Adoptive immunotherapy, notably involving chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells, has obtained Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval as a treatment for various hematological malignancies, demonstrating promising preclinical efficacy against cancers. However, the intricate and resource-intensive autologous cell processing, encompassing collection, expansion, engineering, isolation, and administration, hamper the efficacy of this therapeutic modality.

pmc-11425540.title: 63 General practitioners’ experience, attitudes and needs on providing advice on physical activity to people with chronic ischemic heart disease - A qualitative study (OptiCor study)
pmc-11425540.creator: Alicia Prinz, Verena Leve, Elisabeth Gummersbach, Stefan Wilm, Sabrina Hoppe, Franziska Vogl, Ursula Kirchhof, Anja Neuhaus, Sabrina Kastaun
pmc-11425540.description: PurposeThe German treatment guideline “chronic ischemic/coronary heart disease (IHD)” recommends that general practitioners (GPs) deliver advice on physical activity (PA) to IHD patients. However, the provision of PA advice is inadequately implemented in general practice in Germany. One reason is the lack of medical training in providing PA advice effectively and efficiently. International guidelines recommend such training for GPs.

pmc-12768831.title: PP32 Ultra-Fast Health Technology Assessments: A Descriptive Analysis Of Practices In A Latin American Agency
pmc-12768831.creator: Carla Colaci, Verónica Alfie, Sebastian Garcia Marti, Federico Augustovski, Andres Pichon Riviere, Andrea Alcaraz
pmc-12768831.description: IntroductionHealth technology assessments (HTAs) are essential for evidence-informed decision-making. In urgent clinical scenarios, ultra-rapid HTAs provide concise evaluations to guide patient-specific decisions in 72 hours. The Institute for Clinical Effectiveness and Health Policy (IECS), with over 20 years of experience in HTA, has played a key role in delivering these rapid assessments to support efficient healthcare decisions in Argentina.

pmc-13040301.title: Understanding suicide risk among LGBTQ+ youth in Peru: Findings from a nationwide mental health survey
pmc-13040301.creator: Juan C. Jauregui, Michael Reyes-Diaz, Fran León-Morris, Ronita Nath, Ashley B. Taylor, Kelika A. Konda, Emma Rebecca Wallace, Jose A. Arriola-Vigo
pmc-13040301.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Our findings reveal alarmingly high rates of suicidal ideation and attempts, with over one in three LGBTQ+ youth reporting a suicide attempt in the past year. Critically, we show that risk is associated not only with mental health symptoms such as depression and anxiety, but also with structural and developmental factors, including unmet needs for mental health care, lack of community support and the complex realities of disclosing one’s LGBTQ+ identity in unaccepting environments.

pmc-13087186.title: Biomimetic climbing robot design inspired by geckos and cats for rough wall applications
pmc-13087186.creator: Mohammed K. Jodah, Mofeed Turky Rashid, Ali Hassan Abdulaali, Bilal Naji Alhasnawi, Alžběta Dočekalová, Vladimír Bureš
pmc-13087186.description: This research presents the design of a quadrupedal robot capable of climbing rough surfaces. The robot’s shape, body, arms, and locomotion mechanism were inspired by the gecko, while its limbs were inspired by the limbs cats used to climb trees and grip rough surfaces. The robot has three degrees of freedom.
